analysis.title: 10 for the weekend - 30 Oct 2026 (Dioni Ellinikaki, Equity Franchise Sales)
key_insights: Anecdotal appetite to own risk into year end remains very low, and hedge fund performance remains difficult across strategies.
GS Prime at noon EST on 10/30: Global Fundamental L/S managers down 1.2% on the day and 3.6% MTD. TMT funds down 12.6% MTD, cutting YTD gains to +5.1%.
Systematic managers are down 0.6% on the day and 3.5% MTD but up 16% YTD, and are tracking their first negative month of the year as momentum, crowding and short-term signals stay under pressure.

The mega cap tech debate is shifting to who earns the returns on AI spending and how the investment cycle is financed. Financing constraints forcing capex discipline is the risk, but it is not yet visible in spending intentions.

Eric Sheridan's single stock pick after mega cap results is AMZN. He is constructive on a 12+ month view, citing capacity-constrained AWS demand, triple-digit AI growth and expanding Retail margins. He calls the post-print pullback an attractive entry point.

Midterms: history suggests a risk premium builds into the election and relieves after it. This cycle has other uncertainty (energy, Middle East, AI) that matters more for equity rotation and direction, and not all policy uncertainty clears with the result.
Baskets team flags five midterm trades: ACA subsidies/health insurance affordability, drug pricing, power inflation, government spending and corporate tax.

ACA Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) is the clearest Democratic sweep beneficiary. Power Up America (GSENEPOW) and Grid Infrastructure could outperform if focus shifts to who pays for the grid buildout needed for AI infrastructure.
Corporate Tax (GSPUTAXP) is a valuation risk beyond 2029, though near-term earnings look largely insulated under either midterm outcome.

Jan Hatzius sees downside risk to 2027 growth. DM yield curves are roughly 100bp higher since early 2026, and GS estimates that if the moves persist they could subtract ~0.6% from GDP through weaker housing, consumer spending and investment.
GS expects the growth impulse from the AI boom to peak in late 2026 or early 2027.

European Strategy team says rising debt costs are starting to weigh on margins and capital allocation. It does not expect a systemic credit event but sees a more supportive backdrop for Quality and stronger balance sheets.

European Industrials have derated sharply versus the STOXX 600, which could be an attractive entry point, though the group is tied to the AI trade. Preferred strategy is a barbell of AI beneficiaries (Prysmian, Legrand, VAT, Halma, Atlas Copco) and high ROIC compounders (Rational, Geberit, De'Longhi, Epiroc).
European spec sales best ideas: long Alpha Bank into CMD (Nov 5), Legrand into Q3 (Nov 5), Orange into likely prenotification (November), IMCD through Q3 (Nov 5), Glencore and Bayer into year-end.

ARGX (c.50bn euro market cap): Vyvgart has grown for 19 consecutive quarters, ~20% revenue growth with faster EPS growth. The unexpected Sjogren's setback reset positioning ahead of December EMPASSION data, where Rajan assigns 65% probability of success and ~3% DCF downside if it fails. Added to conviction list.
GS London conferences: Carbonomics (Nov 10), AI & Semis Symposium (Nov 24-25), Industrials & Autos Week (Nov 30-Dec 4).
